label: Seated in: a condition of a being's own nature belongs to what one of its constituents is
term: seated in (SeatedIn Ess Seat x C k)
definition: SeatedIn Ess Seat x C k: the ESSENCE_6 condition C on x's profile lies in x's own nature (Ess x x C) and belongs to what x's constituent k is (Seat x C k, a declared primitive). The constituent k is where the condition is in x, its content being part of what k is. Examples: a triangle's having exactly three sides belongs to what its form is; in a simple being, every condition of its nature belongs to what its one nature is. Non-examples: a condition in another being's nature about x's profile (not own); a negation considered as an item, which is not a real constituent (DEF d6912ecb). Distinguishing conditions: it is not requiring a lack (it relates a condition to a constituent, not a determination to a set of determinations), and it is not realization (it does not say which determinations k is the reality of). Structural properties: none encoded.
